easy.def: A special skill for doing something.
examples: She has a knack for drawing.
He has a knack for fixing things.
I have a knack for it.

more.def: A special ability to do something well, often without effort.
examples: She has a knack for making people laugh.
My uncle has a knack for fixing broken bikes.
It took me a while to get the knack of riding a skateboard.

easy.def: A bag you carry on your back.
examples: I carried a knapsack.
The knapsack is heavy.
He packed his knapsack.

more.def: A bag with straps that you carry on your back, used for carrying things on a hike or to school.
examples: I packed a lunch in my knapsack for the hike.
The hiker carried a knapsack with a map and a water bottle.
He swung his knapsack over his shoulder.

easy.def: The joint in the middle of your leg.
examples: I hurt my knee.
Bend your knee.
She fell on her knee.

more.def: The joint in the middle of the leg that lets it bend.
examples: He scraped his knee on the sidewalk.
Bend your knee to climb the steps.
The baby crawled on her knees.

easy.def: The round bone at the front of your knee.
examples: I hit my kneecap.
The kneecap is round.
My kneecap hurt.

more.def: The flat, round bone at the front of the knee.
examples: He scraped his kneecap when he fell off his bike.
The doctor tapped just below her kneecap.
A pad protects the kneecap in sports.

easy.def: To go down on your knees.
examples: I kneel to pet the cat.
We kneel to plant the seeds.
He knelt to tie his shoe.

more.def: To bend your legs and rest on one or both knees.
examples: She knelt in the garden to pull the weeds.
The player knelt down to catch the low ball.
She kneels by the stream to fill her bottle.
Use a knife to cut the bread.
The knife is sharp.
Be careful with the knife.

more.def: A tool with a sharp blade and a handle, used for cutting.
examples: Dad used a knife to slice the tomatoes.
The knife is kept in a high drawer.
She spread butter with a butter knife.

easy.def: A soldier from long ago who rode a horse.
examples: The knight had a shiny sword.
The knight rode a white horse.
A knight wore heavy metal clothes.

more.def: A soldier of long ago who wore armor, rode a horse, and served a king or queen.
examples: The knight promised to protect the castle.
The queen made the brave soldier a knight.
In the story, the knight fights a dragon.

easy.def: To make cloth by looping yarn with long needles.
examples: Grandma knits scarves.
She knitted a hat.
I want to learn to knit.

more.def: To make cloth or clothing by looping yarn together using two long needles or a machine.
examples: Grandma knitted a warm scarf for me out of soft blue yarn.
She learned to knit by watching her mother.
He knitted a pair of socks for the winter.

easy.def: A round handle on a door or drawer.
examples: Turn the knob.
The knob is round.
A knob on the door.

more.def: A round handle or button that you turn or pull.
examples: Turn the knob to open the door.
The knob on the drawer was shaped like a flower.
He turned the knob to make the radio louder.

easy.def: To hit a door so people know you are there.
examples: Knock on the door.
Someone knocked.
I knock before I go in.

more.def: To hit something, such as a door, to make a sound.
examples: Please knock before you come in.
Someone knocked on the window.
A woodpecker knocked on the tree.

easy.def: To hit something so that it falls.
examples: Do not knock over the cup.
The ball knocked down the pins.
The cat knocked the vase off.

more.def: To hit something so that it falls or moves.
examples: The wind knocked over the garden chair.
Be careful not to knock the lamp off the table.
The ball knocked down all the pins.
That is a knockoff.
The bag is a knockoff.
The knockoff broke.

more.def: A cheap copy of a well-known product.
examples: The bag is a cheap knockoff of the real one.
The toy was a knockoff and broke quickly.
Be careful to buy the real thing, not a knockoff.

easy.def: A place where string or rope is tied.
examples: I tied a knot in my shoelace.
There is a knot in my hair.
Can you undo this knot?

more.def: A fastening made by looping and pulling a string or rope tight.
examples: The sailor tied a strong knot to hold the boat to the dock.
He learned to tie five kinds of knots at camp.
The string was full of knots after the kitten played with it.

easy.def: To have something in your mind as true.
examples: I know my ABCs.
She knows the way home.
Do you know his name?

more.def: To have learned something so that you are sure about it, or to be familiar with a person or place.
examples: I know how to ride a bike without training wheels.
He knew the answer as soon as the teacher asked.
Do you know the girl who just moved in next door?
Reading gives you knowledge.
Books are full of knowledge.
She has a lot of knowledge about bugs.

more.def: What a person knows from learning, studying, or doing things.
examples: Her knowledge of plants helped us pick safe berries.
He shared his knowledge of the stars with us.
Travel gave her knowledge of other ways of life.
The guide is knowledgeable.
A knowledgeable teacher.
She is knowledgeable about birds.

more.def: Having a lot of knowledge or information.
examples: The guide was very knowledgeable about the animals.
The knowledgeable ranger answered every question.
Ask the knowledgeable librarian.

easy.def: A bendy joint in your finger.
examples: I hurt my knuckle.
He tapped with his knuckle.
The knuckle is where the finger bends.

more.def: One of the joints in a finger where it bends.
examples: She knocked on the door with her knuckles.
He scraped his knuckle on the rough wall.
The knuckles on his hand turned white as he held the rope.

easy.def: The bumps on your fingers where they bend.
examples: I cracked my knuckles.
My knuckles are sore.
The knuckles are on my hand.

more.def: The joints in your fingers, where they bend, and the bumps they make at the base of your fingers.
examples: I knocked on the door with my knuckles.
The cold made my knuckles red.
She cracked her knuckles before she played the piano.
